subject: using correlation matrix for sample.cov argument

messages.author: 6855b04443295af7
messages.subject: using correlation matrix for sample.cov argument
parts:
Hello there! 

Does it matter if I use the correlation matrix instead of the covariance matrix in the sample.cov argument?

The result looks identical to me. In fact, even if I don't add the number of sample in the sample.nobs, the results are identical. 

I am just trying to understand how it works. I would imagine that putting a correlation matrix instead of the covariance matrix would lead to slightly different result. 

My understanding is that the estimation is done using variance-covariance matrix instead of correlation matrix. But why would a correlation matrix would end up having the same result?


data(HolzingerSwineford1939)
HSdata<-HolzingerSwineford1939
HSdata <- HSdata[,c(7:15)]
hs_cor <- cor(HSdata)
hs_cov <- cov(HSdata)
hs_cor

model <- 'visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3;
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6;
speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9'

nrow(HSdata)
fit1 <- cfa(model = model, data = HSdata) 
fit2 <- cfa(model = model, sample.cov = hs_cor, sample.nobs = 390) 
fit3 <- cfa(model = model, sample.cov = hs_cov, sample.nobs = 390)
fit4 <- cfa(model = model, sample.cov = hs_cov)

summary(fit1,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE) 
summary(fit2,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE) 
summary(fit3,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE) 
summary(fit4,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE) 

Thank you!
Aiden

messages.author: 71bfb5f1e96782a8
messages.subject: Re: using correlation matrix for sample.cov argument
parts: the correlation is the covariance between standardized variables - so If you put in the correlation matrix this is essentially the same as standardizing all your observed variables beforehand - hence, your parameters are then the same as in the std.ov column. the standardized parameters should be the same for all models.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: using correlation matrix for sample.cov argument
parts: The issue with analyzing s correlation matrix using ML affected the standard errors, not the parameter estimates, and some/ all packages these days employ the needed correction, when a correlation matrix is detected. Lawlry and Maxwell described the problem in their 1972 book.
